name: The hypergraph family
title: The hypergraph family: where group-shaped relations come from
blurb: A hypergraph is not the only way to record who is connected to whom, and it is not always the right one. This section places it among its relatives — directed graphs, bipartite graphs, multigraphs — explains the two equivalent ways of defining a hypergraph, and then spends three cards on the question the literature argues about most: where the hyperedges actually come from. That last question is the one Chapter 7 puts to this paper.
skip_hint: If you can name two different procedures for constructing hyperedges from a dataset that has no hyperedges, skip this section.
